It was just that local African tribes were more willing to sell captives from another tribe they conquered into slavery for the riches of Europe, the Middle-East, and East Asia(sort of like how blacks will kill each other these days to acquire greater control over the drug trade in their community=more money and more women). Native Americans tended to kill their captives, because they just wanted to conquer and dominate the other tribes land.

The particular nature of how African society worked made them better slaves too because they were not necessarily strict Hunter-Gatherers and Pastoralists like Native Americans and Australoids. They practiced slash and burn agricultural methods(very primitive) and in America's case knew how to grow certain goods that could be productive to the colonies(rice is one of them). Anyways, the point is that Africans were probably enslaved because they were considered inferior, but because they were observed as possessing lower cognitive capacities, were not very educated, and were use to hard labor in a subtropical/tropical climate.

It is only today that we now have genetic knowledge that the African race(even closer than Australoids surprisingly; Australoids were probably some very ancient African race connected to Homo Erectus/Denisovans), but their specific branch was broken off from the Pygmy/Bushmen branch of the African race(Pygmies are about 40,000 years separated from other Africans(maybe Neanderthal/modern homo-sapien version of Africans?) and Bushmen 200,000(maybe the African version of the Homo Heidelbergenesis/early Neanderthal?) have chimpanzee/bonobo blood that is most significant then any other part of the human race. Sub-Saharans have actually been infused with more intelligence over the last 10,000 years due to migrations from the Middle-East into Sub-Sahara Africa and some migration over the Sahara(probably when it was less of a desert) from North Africa and possibly points in Europe. This explains why modern Sub-Saharans are on the periphery of being somewhere between borderline retarded and average intelligence with spectrums involved.

I would not say slavery is necessarily the condition of a lower species in human nature(I would not consider Negroes animals per se, only closer to animals genetically), but the lower species are easier to cull, much likelier to be productive(lower cognitive capacity), and much easier to train into mass-producing goods. Colonial Europeans needed this form of labor to ensure the economic success of their enterprise and to ensure their colonies survived.

Most people don't get this. Slavery was driven more by economic necessity and less by racial thinking(that only really came in the 19th century when they had to try to find ways to justify slavery). Anyways, my point is that slave traders, planters, overseers, and the farmers who trained slaves were less "racist" then you think and were merely reacting to what they needed and saw(survival instinct) and if there was racism(regardless of how pseudoscientific) some of it was justified.

I would never personally like to own a slave myself and in modern society(the South would have realized this but kept segregation and anti-miscgeneation laws) slavery is pretty backwards, but you can see why slavery existed and why it could have lasted longer then it did(the end of slavery was less the product of industrialization, but more a product of bourgeoisie humanitarianism). Actually, the lifestyle of the American slave was very similar to poor whites living in America and there were a lot that existed before the Industrial Age when corporate managers could afford to raise wages.

Slaves were only stripped of these rights after Nat Turner rebelled in 1832.
